title: Snap to Pattern
content: **Objective** Activate **Snap to Pattern** to create and edit Internal Shapes and Sewing Lines that accurately fit the point and line. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **Snap to Pattern** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Snap to Pattern** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶**Snap to Pattern** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Snap to Pattern** 2. Create or edit Internal Shapes and Sewing Lines while **Snap to Pattern** is activated. → The Internal Shapes and Sewing Lines snap to the closest point or line. **※ Note:** **Snap to Pattern** is activated by default. Check off the option to deactivate the function.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for activating and utilizing the **Snap to Pattern** feature to accurately create and edit Internal Shapes and Sewing Lines in your design workflow.

title: Apply Linked Editing – Instance Pattern

title: Deactivate (Pattern Only)/Activate
content: **Objective** Deactivated Patterns are considered as nonexistence in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. When deactivating certain Patterns, the Simulation speed gets faster as it excludes them from calculation. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Deactivate (Pattern Only)** / **Activate** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Deactivate (Pattern Only)** / **Activate** **Operation** 1. title: Offset Pattern Outline
content: **Offset Pattern Outline** * **Offset Pattern Outline ** \- Extend the Pattern outline while maintaining the shape of the Pattern. * **Offset a Segment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=89K2uzTOe4c \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022571447/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment of a Pattern and select **Offset Pattern Outline** from the pop-up menu. \- The Offset Pattern Outline Window will appear. * **Distance** : set how much the Offset Pattern Outline will be apart from the original Pattern outline. * **Number of Offsets** : set how many offsets will be duplicated. * **Total Distance** : total distance equals to the result of Distance multiplying Number of Offsets. * **Create Internal Line** : toggle on to convert the original Pattern outline as an Internal Line. * **Extend Side Segments** : toggle on the option to extend adjacent Pattern outlines, maintaining their original slope. * **Default Corner, Right Angled Corner, and Unfilled Corner** : decide how corners of the offset Pattern outline will be shaped. This option is not used when offsetting a segment. * **Offset an Entire Pattern ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_93HaonYlfQ \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022571447/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022571767/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a Pattern and select **Offset Pattern Outline** from the pop-up menu. \- The Offset Pattern Outline Window will appear. * **Distance** : set how much the Offset Pattern Outline will be apart from the original pattern outline. * **Number of Offsets** : set how many offsets will be duplicated. * **Total Distance** : total distance equals to the result of Distance multiplying Number of Offsets. * **Create Internal Line** : toggle on to convert the original Pattern outline as an Internal Line. * **Extend Side Segments** : toggle on the option to extend adjacent Pattern outlines, maintaining their original slope. This is not used when offsetting an entire Pattern. * **Default Corner, Right Angled Corner, and Unfilled Corner** : decide how corners of the offset Pattern outline will be shaped. The Pattern outline will be offset based on the setting.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Offset Pattern Outline feature to extend and modify pattern outlines while preserving their original shapes in a 2D design environment.

title: Segment Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Segment Sewing Establish Sewing Lines Directional Notches Divide Sewing Lines Based on Notches **Segment Sewing** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xlE08VVux5M \- Establish Sewing Lines on segments, split by points, to connect Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png) **Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing.** ** Establish Sewing Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zxXoWyYlINc \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png) **Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on a segment on a Pattern to establish the first half of the Sewing Line. \- Then, hover the mouse over the segment where the second half of the Sewing Line will be placed to. \- Drag the mouse to alter the direction of the Directional Notch as desired. \- Click on the segment to establish the second half of the Sewing Line. \- A pair of Sewing Lines is completed. \- The Sewing Line difference will hover over the mouse cursor. \- When the Sewing Line difference is larger than 1mm, the value will appear in red to alert users. **Directional Notches** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6RfaA1mApNk \- The direction of the Directional Notches can be changed by moving the mouse on the Sewing Lines. \- To reset the Directional Notches on a pair of Sewing Lines, hit the ESC key or the Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard. **Divide Sewing Lines Based On Nothches(ver4.1.0)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jvyaHp-R5c0 \- Now sewing lines can be created snapping on notches, without adding segment points. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png)**Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Establish sewing lines based on notches. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on segment sewing techniques, including establishing sewing lines, using directional notches, and dividing sewing lines, enhanced with instructional YouTube videos for practical understanding.

title: [3D Tool] Segment Sewing
content: ### **Objective** In the 3D window, easily establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001250948/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001250948/_______.png) **Segment Sewing ** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Navigate to the 3D window. 3. Click once on the Pattern Outline to establish the first half of the seam. 4. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. → When moving the mouse cursor, a blue point appears indicating the length of the first half of the seam. 5. When the mouse cursor is moved close to the blue point, the Sewing Line snaps to the point (ver5.1.0). Drag the mouse to make the the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. **※ Note** * When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more detail, please reference [M:N Segment Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001771067).
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for establishing Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes in both 2D and 3D windows within the CLO 3D software.

content: **Divide Sewing Lines Based On Nothches_ver.4.1.0** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cRoEkhuhuCg \- Now sewing lines can be created snapping on notches, without adding segment points. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png)**Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Establish sewing lines based on notches.

title: Edit Notch Properties
content: **List of Contents** Notch Properties Edit Notch Properties Notch Length **Notch Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yt0bkOa9zaA ** \- Edit properties of a Notch as needed. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026559547/mceclip0.png) **Notch** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** ** Edit Notch Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRYwtK0Uw6U ** \- Select the Notch to be modified. \- The properties of the selected Notch appear in the Property Editor. * **Name YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1nwU8XVE3EU **\- Rename the Notch. * **Type YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iz3kah5lC28 ** \- Choose the type of the Notch. * **Angle YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B6dieNf2Ynw ** \- Set the degree of angle for the Notch. * **Perpendicular** \- The Notch is placed perpendicular to its segment. * **Custom** \- Decide the angle of the Notch based on its segment. * **Direction YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=te-WS1ugNxQ ** \- This option only appears when a Notch is created in a corner. \- Decided the direction of the Notch. * **Point (Center)** \- The Notch is created at the center of the corner. * **Segment 1** \- The Notch is created towards a segment. * **Segment 2** \- The Notch is created towards the other segment. * **Flip YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YIk80LPWgQ8 ** \- The Notch is created on the other side of the segment. **Notch Length_ver.5.0.0 and Above** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V5GvUlF-xxQ \- Edit Notch length as desired. content: **List of Contents** Select Move **Objective** Select or move notches. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![notch.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024295548/notch.png) **Notch** ** Operation** **Select** 1. title: Notch
content: **List of Contents** Notch Create Notch Select Notch Move Notch Delete Notch Notch on Seam Allowance Notch Display Type **Notch YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3ey_Nu931a8 ** \- Create, select, move, and delete Notches on Pattern outlines. \- Select the Notch tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** ** Create Notch** * **Create Manually YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sGcWMX3P-Hg ** \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline or Internal Line where a notch should be added. \- A red point appears on the segment where the mouse is hovering over. \- Click on the segment to create a Notch and it is automatically selected and highlighted in yellow. * **Create with Specific Numbers YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CHHpoggTkYU ** \- To create a Notch on a specific position, right click on a segment where a notch is desired to be added. \- The Notch window appears allowing you to specify location. * **Split into Two Lines ** \- The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. * **Split by Length** \- Divide the selected line into multiple segments according to the desired length of each segment. \- **Segment Length** : Enter the segment length, which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select Reverse Direction. \- **Number of Segments** : Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. \- **Direction** : Reverse the direction that points are added. * **Uniform Split** \- Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into next to the **Number of Segments** option. title: Create Notch
content: **List of Contents** Create Manually Create with Specific Values Add Point to Notch **Objective** Create notch on Pattern outlines as desired to improve sewing accuracy. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![notch.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024295408/notch.png) **Notch** **Operation** **Create Manually** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline where the notch is to be added. → A notch is created and the [notch properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013369268-Edit-Notch-Properties) appear in the Property Editor. **※Note:** Right-click on a point with Edit Pattern or Edit Curve Point tool (ver 6.1) and click Add Notch, a notch is created at the point **Create with Specific Values ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Right-click on the Pattern outline where notches should be added to access the pop-up window. Then, type in the desired values referring to the table below. ****** ****** **Split Into Two Lines** | Line 1 / Line 2 | The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as Line 1, and the longer side is indicated as Line 2. Enter the desired value in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. ---|---|--- Ratio | The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. This function is often used split a line into two identical segments or to add a point at its 33.3%. **Split by Length** **** | Segment Length | Enter the segment length which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select **Reverse Direction**. Number of Segments | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. It is set as 2 by default. Direction | Reverse the direction that points are added. **Uniform Split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. 3. The notches are created based on the chosen options. **Add Point to Notch** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the notch and click Add Point to Notch. → A straight point is added to the notch. **※Note:** If there is a seam allowance in the pattern in which the notch was created, the notch also appears in the seam allowance. In addition, if a notch is created in the corner of a pattern with seam allowance, the notch appears randomly only in one seam allowance of both seams. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for creating notches on pattern outlines to enhance sewing accuracy, detailing various methods and options for customization.

content: **List of Contents** Internal Ellipse Create **Internal EllipseYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_0FCRmB9heg ** \- Create ellipse or circle within a Pattern. \- Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Ellipse** \- 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Circle.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001203908/Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Circle.png)**Internal Ellipse** **Create** * **Create**** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TTXryZsJjpU** \- Click and drag within a Pattern to create an ellipse in the 2D window. \- To create a circle, hold down the Shift key while click and drag. * **Create with Specific ValuesYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4jKzfBVvA2k** \- Click within a Pattern to create an ellipse with specific values. \- The Create Ellipse window appears. * Size Diameter: Set width and height of an ellipse. title: Create Custom Texture Image
content: **List of Contents** Scan Fabric Create Repeat Match DPI (Resolution) Match Color **Objective** Create various custom texture images and apply to fabrics to express variety of fabric in CLO. There are four steps total to create a custom texture image: Scanning Fabric, Making Repeat, Matching DPI (Resolution), and Adjusting Color. In order to make custom texture image, image editing software, such as [Pixplant](https://www.pixplant.com/index.php), [Adobe Photoshop](http://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop.html) is needed. **Operation** **Scan Fabric** Scan fabrics to digitize real world fabrics. If scanner is not available, use digital camera or cellphone camera instead. 1. Prepare the scanner, digital camera, or cellphone camera. 2. Spread the fabric flat on an even surface and photograph it, aligning the grainline perpendicular to the scanner or the camera's corner of the screen. 3. Send the image to the computer. **Create Repeat ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3bf4ZCaMQeo When a fabric is observed carefully, you can find the structure which repeats like a pattern and the structure of the fabric is often indicated as a Repeat. To express a fabric's texture, create a Repeat using the scanned image. Ways to create a Repeat differs depending on the characteristics of each fabric. Please refer to the appropriate guideline as needed. **When Fabric Structure is Small and Irregular** 1. Launch [PixPlant](https://www.pixplant.com/download.php). If PixPlant is not available, please use other image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop. 2. Left click on the Add button on the right top corner and locate the scanned image to load. 3. Left click on the Straighten Seed > Click to Edit button, then select a clean part of the scanned image. 4. Click the Generate button to create a Repeat. 5. The area inside the square box in the Texture Canvas window represents the Repeat. Repeat procedure 3 and 4 until the desired Repeat is achieved. 6. To recreate some portion of the Repeat, drag to select the desired part within the square box in the Texture Canvas window. 7. When the desired Repeat is achieved, click Save. **When Fabric Structure is Big and Regular** 1. Launch [Adobe Photoshop](http://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop.html) or other image editing software. 2. Find the smallest repeated area on the scanned image. 3. Select and cut the repeated area. 4. Copy, paste and align repeated area to check if they align naturally. 5. When the repeated area does not align properly, showing grid lines, edit the image to make it align more smoothly. 6. When the desired image is achieved, save the image. **※ Note:** When creating Repeats for fabrics with transparency, please select and delete the Repeat image's background and save it as PNG. **Match DPI (Resolution)** In order to match the image ratio of the Repeat and the real world fabric, adjust DPI (Resolution). 1. Launch Adobe Photoshop. 2. Open previously created Repeat. 3. Navigate and select Main Menu > Image > Image Size. 4. When a pop-up window appears, toggle on the Resample Image option and adjust the DPI (Resoultion) value respective to the DPI (Resolution) of the original scanned image. Open the original scanned image in Adobe Photoshop to check its DPI (Resolution) value. 5. Save the Repeat. **Match Color** Match the Repeat's color respective to the real world fabric. Occasionally, photographing fabric may distort the fabric's real color. In these cases, after creating a Repeat image, adjust its color, matching the color to the original fabric's color. Open the Repeat in an image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop and adjust color as needed. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Create custom fabric textures for CLO by scanning, editing, and matching the DPI and color of real-world fabrics through a detailed four-step process.

title: How can I express embroidery in CLO?
content: **Question** How can I express embroidery in CLO? **Answer** There are three possible ways to express embroidery in CLO differ by the purpose and the situation. With Scanned Embroidery Without Scanned Embroidery** ** **With Scanned Embroidery** When there is a scanned image of embroidery, use the [Graphic tools](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000483967) in CLO to express embroidery. However, as expressing thick embroidery and flat embroidery methods are different, please refer to the appropriate guide below. ** Express Embroidery with Thickness ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=unFS2e09qd8 To express embroidery with thickness, please refer to below instruction. 1. [Create](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000511208) a rectangle Pattern in the 2D window. 2. Apply a new fabric to the Pattern and add texture. 3. [Create Internal Lines](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000481707) in the shape of embroidery on the Pattern and cut. 4. Delete unnecessary Pattern and duplicate the Pattern outline as an Internal Shape to the 3D Garment Pattern. 5. [Sew](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000641848-%EC%9E%AC%EB%B4%89%EC%84%A0-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) the embroidery Pattern to the 3D Garment. 6. Click on the fabric item applied to the embroidery Pattern in the Object Browser and change its Preset as Fusible Rigid. Also, change the Particle Distance to 5. ** Express Flat Embroidery ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cII93rWvu3M Use the [Graphic tools](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000483967) to add the embroidery image to the 3D Garment in order to express embroidery with no thickness. **Without Scanned Embroidery **** **If there is no scanned image of embroidery, use the image editing tool such as Adobe Photoshop to express embroidery effects. Then, refer to guides from the With Scanned Embroidery section. You may search how to express embroidery in image editing tools online or take a look at the reference we found below! [Video Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HbZac9imfZA) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover various methods to express embroidery in CLO, whether using scanned images or image editing tools, tailored to your specific needs and desired effects.

title: Create Custom Texture Image for Curved Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Using Adobe Photoshop Using Adobe Illustrator **Objective** Create custom texture image for curved pattern such as neckband. Use curved texture image when expressing lace or biz trims. **Operation** **Using Adobe Photoshop ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jte2rUXzrIw Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Photoshop. 1. [Create a Repeat](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012228067) of real world fabric. 2. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. 3. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. 4. Take a screenshot of the pattern. 5. Launch Adobe Photoshop and open both screenshot and Repeat image. 6. Place the Repeat image on top of the pattern image. 7. Use the [Warp](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/warp-images-shapes-paths.html) function to transform the Repeat image respective to the pattern. 8. Open a new window in Adobe Photoshop. 9. Select, copy, and paste the modified Repeat image to the newly opened window. 10. Save the modified Repeat image as PNG and be mindful to set the canvas size bigger than the modified Repeat image for easy application and modification in CLO. 11. [Apply](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388) the modified Repeat image to the pattern and [adjust](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002680348) as needed to place the graphic properly. **Using Adobe Illustrator ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C2b2OfG33V8 **** Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Illustrator. 1. [Create a Repeat](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012228067) of real world fabric. 2. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. 3. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. 4. Take a screenshot of the pattern. 5. Launch Adobe Illustrator and open both screenshot and Repeat image. 6. Trace the pattern image with the [pen](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/drawing-pen-curvature-or-pencil.html) tool. 7. Select the Repeat image and [add as a pattern brush](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/how-to/illustrator-create-pattern-brush.html). 8. Select and copy the longest segment of the traced pattern and apply the pattern brush created in procedure 6. 9. Place the traced pattern on top of the segment with pattern brush applied. 10. Select both pattern and segment, right click and select Make Clipping Mask. The segment with pattern brush applied will be clipped based on the pattern shape. 11. Select the clipped pattern, navigate and select Main Menu > File > Export Selection. 12. Designate the saving path, file name and save as PNG. 13. [Apply](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388) the modified Repeat image to the pattern and [adjust](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002680348) as needed to place the graphic properly. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for creating custom texture images for curved patterns using Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Illustrator, ideal for enhancing designs such as neckbands and lace trims.

title: Garment Rendering Style
content: **List of Contents** Garment Rendering Style Textured Surface Thick Textured Surface Transparent Surface Monochrome Surface Mesh Random Colored Surface **Garment Rendering Style** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5GcJjTtVxhk \- Check the tightness of 3D Garments with the color scale. \- Hover over the third icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D window. ** Textured Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=smqtYtFzLPs \- Only the front side of the 3D Garment will appear in its original color and the back side will appear darker to indicate the sides of the fabric. \- The Garment thickness will not be expressed. **Thick Textured Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Z-FXrLR7Yk \- Both front and back sides of the 3D Garment will appear in their original color and the Garment thickness will be expressed. **Transparent Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2GCZ6r3TPgI \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent. **Monochrome Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3hg2aA4YMvc \- The 3D Garment will appear in black and white. \- The Garment thickness will not be expressed. **Mesh** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JUPrj9c6mGM \- The 3D Garment will appear in the mesh structure. **Random Color Surface_ver5.0.0 and Above** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cK1d2Ohd5E0 \- Select the **Random Color Surface** icon to distinguish Patterns as they are assigned to random colors. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore a comprehensive guide to various garment rendering styles, complete with instructional videos and detailed descriptions to enhance your 3D design experience.

title: Fabric_Color
content: **List of Contents** Color Change color Change color with Eyedropper **Color** \- Change the color of the fabric. ** Change Color** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BaLA0rWayII \- When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected item’s properties will appear in the Property Editor. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. \- Click on the Color chip to open the Color window to assign the desired Color to the selected item. \- Click the desired Color. The selected Color will be applied to the item. \- Click OK to complete. **Change Color with Eyedropper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bYoJXtoD0VE \- When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected item’s properties will appear in the Property Editor. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. \- Click on the Color chip to open the Color window. \- Select the **Eyedropper** tool. \- Drag the mouse cursor outside the Color window. When the cursor changes to an Eyedropper, click on the spot anywhere in the window to extract the desired color. \- The color of the selected spot will appear in the Color window. \- Select OK to complete. \- The chosen Color will be assigned to the selected item. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for changing colors of various design elements using both standard color selection and the Eyedropper tool.
